cards.back: Automation = executing a single task; orchestration = coordinating multiple tools and steps in a workflow.
User provisioning, resource provisioning, desired state management, anomaly detection, ticket management.
Consistent, rapid creation, permission assignment, and revocation at onboarding and offboarding.
Automated, reproducible creation of VMs, containers, or cloud accounts.
Comparing actual state to expected state and automatically remediating any configuration drift.
Automated analysis of logs and baselines; creating, assigning, and closing tickets without manual entry.
Guardrails, automation logic, process engineering, complexity, financial considerations, process risks, deployment.
Limit that bounds the scope, duration, or impact of an automated action and requires approval when needed.
Conditions, step order, error handling, and edge cases of a playbook.

Errors execute at machine speed: test, roll out gradually, monitor, and plan for rollback.

Conversational assistant to query documentation or help draft analyses.
Anticipating incidents or outages from trends and weak signals.
Behavioral baselines enriched by machine learning to better detect anomalies.
AI capable of planning and executing a sequence of actions autonomously; requires guardrails.
Time savings, continuous enforcement of expected configuration, fewer repetitive tasks.
Efficiency/time saving, enforcing baselines, continuous improvements, productivity, reduced downtime, increased proactivity.
